deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §6.3 of Grothendieck's notes on crystalline and stratifying cohomology. The previous page computes H*(X_cris, F) by a Čech–Alexander type complex built from formal completions Y^{ν+1}_{/X} of an embedding X ⊂ Y with Y smooth over S. From this it shows invariance under a nilpotent immersion X_0 ⊂ X: if F comes from F_0 on X_0,cris, then H*(X_cris, F) ≅ H*(X_0,cris, F_0).

This page specialises the result.
1. Take X smooth over S; one may then take Y = X.
2. Take a nilpotent immersion S_0 → S and set X_0 = X ×_S S_0, so X_0 → X is a nilpotent immersion.
3. Regard X_0 as an S-scheme, not an S_0-scheme, when forming X_0,cris. Invariance then gives H*(X_cris/S, O) ≅ H*(X_0,cris/S, O).
4. Consequence: the left side, i.e. the cohomology of any smooth lift X/S, depends up to canonical isomorphism only on the smooth S_0-scheme X_0. It does not depend on the chosen lift.
5. When S has characteristic 0, divided powers impose no condition, so crystalline cohomology is infinitesimal cohomology. By the formal Poincaré lemma the left side is canonically H*(X_zar, Ω•_{X/S}).
6. Hence one gets an intrinsic definition of de Rham cohomology for a possibly singular variety, or for an arbitrary morphism f: X → S in characteristic 0. It is defined as the cohomology of the crystalline/infinitesimal site of X over S, with no smoothness or lifting needed.
7. Bracketed refinement: one can even define the hypercohomology H*(Ω•_{X/S}) as an 'absolute' object (a crystal) on S. This gives its extension to all infinitesimal neighbourhoods of S, not only those that retract onto S. This is in effect the crystal structure of relative de Rham cohomology, i.e. the Gauss–Manin connection, extended to arbitrary thickenings.

Purpose: to show that de Rham cohomology is a crystalline invariant of the reduction X_0. It is the foundational rigidity/independence-of-lift statement behind crystalline cohomology and algebraic de Rham cohomology of singular varieties.
errors: In mixed or positive characteristic the identification H*(X_cris/S) = H*(X_0,cris/S) needs the ideal of S_0 in S to carry divided powers compatible with the base PD-structure (or a stratifying/infinitesimal setting). The page states it only for a 'nilpotent immersion' without spelling this out. The characteristic-0 conclusion is unaffected.

The identification with H*(X_zar, Ω•_{X/S}) is valid only in characteristic 0, as the page correctly restricts. In characteristic p, infinitesimal (stratifying) cohomology is not de Rham cohomology. No actual error, but the scope should be noted.

ideas.what: Crystalline cohomology of a smooth lift X/S of X_0/S_0 depends only on X_0 (independence of lift via nilpotent invariance of the crystalline site)
ideas.modern_name: Nilpotent/PD invariance of crystalline cohomology; independence of de Rham cohomology of the lift
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Characteristic-0 comparison: infinitesimal/crystalline cohomology of smooth X/S equals algebraic de Rham cohomology; used to define de Rham cohomology of singular varieties and arbitrary morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Infinitesimal site / algebraic de Rham cohomology of singular varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter to Atiyah and 'Crystals' notes), Hartshorne (1975)
ideas.where_published: 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968)

ideas.what: Relative de Rham cohomology H*(Ω•_{X/S}) as an absolute object (crystal) on S, extending to all infinitesimal neighbourhoods of S, not only retracting ones
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline nature of Gauss–Manin connection / de Rham cohomology as a crystal on S
ideas.where_published: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes for the crystalline cohomology lectures. Every idea on the page — independence of the lift, the characteristic-0 de Rham comparison, de Rham cohomology of singular varieties via the infinitesimal site, and the crystal on S — appears in Grothendieck's 1966–68 published 'Crystals' and de Rham papers and in Berthelot's work.
